learning_outcomes.text: Have a general overview of electronics in its different branches and fields of application.
Understand the behavior, characteristics, and main applications of electronic devices.
Analyze and understand the operation of circuits in which electronic components are present.
Handle datasheets of integrated circuits for analog or digital applications and use some of them in basic assemblies.
Handle laboratory instrumentation and electronic equipment and perform static and temporal measurements in electronic circuits.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I: BASIC CONCEPTS OF ELECTRONICS
TOPIC 6: THE IDEAL OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIER. LINEAR AND NON-LINEAR APPLICATIONS.
TOPIC 7: FUNDAMENTALS OF DIGITAL DESIGN. BOOLEAN ALGEBRA.
TOPIC 9: DIGITAL INTEGRATED CIRCUITS: LOGIC FAMILIES.
Practice 1 - Handling laboratory equipment (I). Power supply and multimeter.
Practice 2 - Handling laboratory equipment (II). Function generator and oscilloscope.
Practice 6 - Assembly and testing of electronic circuits.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum score of 5.0 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and practical blocks. The theoretical grade is calculated as (0.35 x T1) + (0.35 x T2) + (0.30 x T3), and the practical grade is P1. The final grade is (0.9 x Theory) + (0.1 x Practices), otherwise the grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, students must achieve a minimum of 5.0 out of 10 in both theoretical and practical parts, calculated as (0.35 x B1) + (0.35 x B2) + (0.30 x B3) for theory, and the practical exam score for practices. The final grade is (0.9 x Theory) + (0.1 x Practices), otherwise the grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. Practical grades from the ordinary call are retained for extraordinary calls if the student is considered "presented" (participated in >50% of evaluable tests).
